dct_description_sm: Plastic debris is commonly ingested by seabirds, even in high Arctic waters, but only recently has attention turned to what the impacts may be of this ingested pollution. Since 2003 the Arctic seabird team has worked to identify which northern marine bird species are vulnerable to ingesting marine plastic pollution. Importantly, there is increasing evidence that once marine plastic pollution is in the gut of seabirds, contaminants adsorbed to plastics are released, which may have negative effects on exposed wildlife. The aim of this project is to contribute to our growing understanding of the link between macro-contaminants (i.e. plastics) and micro-contaminants (i.e. chemicals), and to improve our understanding of how plastic pollution may act as a source and long-range vector for contaminants to enter Arctic ecosystems and cycle within marine animals.
dct_title_s: Plastics as a vector of contaminants in Arctic seabirds, Labrador Sea and Lancaster Sound
